express_entry.summary: IRCC holds category-based Express Entry draws for 'Healthcare and social services occupations'. Registered nurses (NOC 31301) qualify if they have at least 12 months of full-time (or equal part-time) work in that one occupation within the last 3 years, in Canada or abroad, and also meet a federal program (e.g. Federal Skilled Worker). Draws are not on a fixed schedule; invited candidates must meet the minimum CRS score of that round. In 2026 there have been three healthcare draws so far.
express_entry.noc: 31301 (Registered nurses and registered psychiatric nurses); 31302 for nurse practitioners

points.summary: You need at least 65 points (age, English, work experience, qualifications, partner, Australian study and more) to lodge an Expression of Interest in SkillSelect. For the 189 visa, Home Affairs invites the highest-ranked EOIs per occupation in periodic rounds; ties are broken by date of effect. State nomination adds 5 points (190) or 15 points (491) and follows each state's own rules.

sid.summary: The Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) replaced the Temporary Skill Shortage visa in December 2024. It has three streams: Core Skills (occupation on the Core Skills Occupation List and salary at or above the Core Skills Income Threshold), Specialist Skills (higher salary threshold), and Labour Agreement. Stay is up to 4 years, with no age limit, and it can lead to permanent residence through the Employer Nomination Scheme (186). The Core Skills Income Threshold was reported as AUD 79,499 for applications lodged from 1 July 2026. Many public health services (for example SA Health) sponsor nurses for roles they cannot fill locally.

notes: ANMAC skills assessment is separate from Ahpra registration; a positive ANMAC result does not mean you can register to practice.
Home Affairs still uses ANZSCO codes for migration as of mid-2026; a move to the new OSCA classification is expected but not yet adopted.
State nomination programs reset each July and allocations are often used up before June; check official state pages often.
Employers such as WA Health sponsor only experienced nurses in areas of critical shortage, and will not sponsor visas for bridging courses or English testing.

green_list.tier: Tier 1 – Straight to Residence (no prior NZ work time needed)
green_list.occupation: Registered Nurse (Green List Tier 1 health roles, e.g. Registered Nurse (Aged Care) and Registered Nurse (Critical Care and Emergency) – check the INZ Green List roles search for your exact occupation)
requirements: Full New Zealand registration with the Nursing Council and a current Annual Practising Certificate
Job offer or current job in the Green List Tier 1 role with an accredited employer
Job must be permanent or fixed-term for at least 12 months (or contracts totalling at least 6 months)
Pay at least the rate set for that Tier 1 role; if none is set, at least the median wage (NZD 35.00/hour, from 9 March 2026)
Aged 55 or younger when you apply
Good health, good character and English ability; genuine relationship with any partner or children included
green_list.processing: 80% of Straight to Residence applications decided within 3 months (INZ); fee from NZD 6,450

aewv.summary: Temporary work visa for a full-time job (at least 30 hours/week) with an accredited employer that has an approved job check. Since 10 March 2025 the AEWV no longer requires the median wage: the employer must pay at least the NZ minimum wage and the NZ market rate for the role. Skill evidence is not needed if you hold the required occupational registration or are Green List eligible. Valid up to 5 years; fee from NZD 1,540; 80% processed within 5 weeks. Partners and children apply for their own visas, and supporting dependent children has an income threshold.

smc.summary: Residence visa needing 6 skilled resident points from one of: qualification (4–6), NZ occupational registration (3–6, by length of training), or income (3–6 at 1.5x, 2x or 3x the SMC wage threshold), topped up by up to 3 points for NZ skilled work (1 point per year, max 3). You also need a skilled job in NZ, age 55 or under, English, health and character. Fee from NZD 6,450. Nurses who qualify for Green List Tier 1 usually use Straight to Residence instead.

notes: Registration comes first: you cannot apply for Straight to Residence as a nurse until you are registered with the Nursing Council.
Health New Zealand is an accredited employer and runs a Health Immigration Service for candidates; it warns that its recruitment never asks candidates for money.
The immigration median wage rose to NZD 35.00/hour on 9 March 2026; it matters for residence, not for AEWV pay since March 2025.
A National Occupation List (NOL) is replacing ANZSCO for AEWV; NOL codes are not used for SMC, so check which code your visa uses.
